name: Letybo
summary: A newer FDA-approved botulinum toxin for frown lines, also sold as Botulax in Korea.
lead: Letybo is a brand of letibotulinumtoxinA, a botulinum toxin type A injectable. It is used to soften frown lines between the eyebrows (glabellar lines) and, in routine practice, in the upper face more broadly. The US Food and Drug Administration approved it for glabellar lines in February 2024, according to Wikipedia.

name: Relfydess
summary: Galderma's ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin for frown lines, supported by a Phase 3 trial.
lead: Relfydess (relabotulinumtoxinA) is a ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin type A made by Galderma, developed with a technology the company calls PEARL to produce a complex-free formulation. Unlike freeze-dried toxins, it does not require reconstitution.

name: Nabota
summary: Daewoong's botulinum toxin, sold as Nabota in Korea and Jeuveau in the US, studied for wrinkles, masseters and spasticity.
lead: Nabota (prabotulinumtoxinA) is a botulinum toxin type A made by Daewoong Pharmaceutical of South Korea. The same toxin is marketed in the US as Jeuveau, sold by Evolus and manufactured by Daewoong, according to Wikipedia.

name: Botulax / Hutox / Meditoxin
summary: Korean botulinum toxin brands used abroad for wrinkles and jaw slimming, with trials mostly against Botox.
lead: Botulax, Hutox and Meditoxin are botulinum toxin type A products from South Korean makers. Botulax contains letibotulinumtoxinA, and Meditoxin (also marketed as Neuronox) was developed by Medy-Tox. They are used for wrinkles and, in studies, for masseter hypertrophy, spasticity and blepharospasm.

name: Trap Botox (Barbie Botox)
summary: Toxin injected into the trapezius to make the neck look longer; a 2024 systematic review exists, cosmetic data are thin.
lead: Trap Botox, popularly called "Barbie Botox", is the injection of botulinum toxin into the trapezius muscle, aimed at relaxing the muscle so the neck appears longer and the shoulder line slimmer. It is an off-label cosmetic use of a toxin.

name: Juvederm Voluma
summary: Firm hyaluronic acid cheek and chin filler from Allergan; temporary volume with studies behind it, plus filler-class risks.
lead: Juvéderm Voluma (marketed in the US as Juvéderm Voluma XC) is a cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal filler made by Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company. It is a 20 mg/mL gel built with the company's Vycross cross-linking technology and, in the XC version, contains 0.3% lidocaine.  It is designed for deep injection to restore or add volume, and is best known as a cheek and midface filler.
claims: Cheek and chin filler can approximate the effect of implants without surgery
Fillers are safe because they can be dissolved

name: Juvederm Volux
summary: Allergan's firm HA gel for chin and jawline, with published trials and little community data beyond anecdotes.
lead: Juvéderm Volux (VYC-25L; Volux XC in the US) is a cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) filler from Allergan, made with Vycross technology and positioned as a firm gel for the chin and jawline.  A 2020 study describes it as designed to restore and create facial volume, and expert consensus authors describe it as a first-in-class Vycross filler for chin and lower-third remodelling.
claims: Volux gives results similar to Voluma for the chin but with more discomfort

name: Juvederm Volbella
summary: Allergan's fine HA filler for lips and under-eye hollows, backed by randomized trials, with reports of late reactions in the tear-trough area.
lead: Juvéderm Volbella (VYC-15L; Volbella XC with lidocaine) is a low-concentration cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) filler from Allergan, made with Vycross technology and used for fine lines and delicate areas, chiefly the lips and perioral region and the under-eye hollow (infraorbital) area.

name: Restylane Defyne / Lyft / Kysse
summary: Galderma's HA filler family for cheeks (Lyft), contour and lines (Defyne) and lips (Kysse), with randomized trials for Lyft.
lead: Restylane Defyne, Restylane Lyft and Restylane Kysse are hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers in the Restylane range made by Galderma, which acquired the original developer Q-Med in 2011 according to Grokipedia.  Lyft is a large-gel-particle product for cheeks and midface (and hands); Defyne is a flexible gel for smile lines and facial contouring; Kysse is for lip enhancement and perioral lines.

name: RHA fillers (Teoxane)
summary: Teoxane's flexible HA gels built for moving areas like the mouth, with randomized perioral and under-eye trials.
lead: RHA (Resilient Hyaluronic Acid) fillers are cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) products from the Swiss company Teoxane, marketed as Teosyal RHA outside the US and RHA Redensity in the US. They were developed to hold up in dynamic areas of the face that move with expression, such as around the mouth.

name: Belotero Balance
summary: Merz's soft, cohesive HA filler for fine lines and under-eye hollows, with a 12-month randomized comparison and modest forum chatter.
lead: Belotero Balance is a hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal filler from Merz that uses cohesive polydensified matrix (CPM) technology, designed to integrate smoothly into the skin. It is used for fine lines and superficial areas such as nasolabial folds, and has been studied for the under-eye (infraorbital) hollow.
claims: Filler can stand in for or precede major surgery

name: Ellansé (PCL filler)
summary: A PCL microsphere collagen-stimulating filler marketed for longer-lasting facial volume, backed by small prospective studies.
lead: Ellansé is a brand of injectable dermal filler whose active component is polycaprolactone (PCL), a biodegradable polyester, formulated as microspheres suspended in a carboxymethylcellulose gel carrier. It belongs to the class of collagen stimulators (biostimulators): rather than only adding volume itself, it is described as prompting the body to lay down new collagen around the microspheres.

name: Aquamid / polyacrylamide filler
summary: A permanent polyacrylamide hydrogel filler that does not absorb, with a five-year study behind it and documented late reactions.
lead: Aquamid is a brand of injectable polyacrylamide hydrogel (PAAG), a non-biodegradable water-based gel with a cross-linked polyacrylamide network, used for soft-tissue augmentation. Polyacrylamide hydrogels are classed among the permanent or non-resorbable fillers, in contrast with hyaluronic acid fillers, which the body gradually breaks down.

name: Autologous fat transfer to face
summary: Using your own harvested fat as a face filler; well-established surgical technique, with variable retention and rare serious complications.
lead: Autologous fat transfer to the face, also called facial fat grafting or lipofilling, is a surgical procedure in which a person's own fat is harvested from another part of the body, processed, and injected into the face to restore volume or alter contour. It is used for facial rejuvenation, where volume loss is recognised as a component of ageing, and for reconstructive and contouring purposes.

name: Jawline filler
summary: Hyaluronic acid or CaHA injected along the mandible to sharpen the jawline without surgery; trials are registered but risks include rare vascular events.
lead: Jawline filler refers to the injection of a dermal filler, most often a hyaluronic acid (HA) or calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) product, along the mandible to add definition or volume to the jaw angle, jawline or chin area. It is a non-surgical option used to accentuate a sharper or wider lower face, to address a jawline contour deficit, and to reduce the look of jowls.
claims: Jawline filler gives a visible sharper jaw once swelling settles
Filler is a worthwhile ongoing investment compared with surgery
Filler can be dissolved if unwanted

name: Temple filler
summary: Filler placed in the temple hollow to smooth the side of the forehead; common, but the area is anatomically risky and most research is anatomical.
lead: Temple filler is the injection of a dermal filler, most commonly hyaluronic acid (HA), into the temporal fossa to restore volume in temporal hollowing, a concavity at the side of the forehead that is associated with ageing and facial thinness. Practitioners describe it as improving facial balance and, by softening the hollow, giving the upper face a smoother outline.

name: Tear trough filler
summary: HA filler placed in the under-eye hollow as a subtle, quick alternative to eyelid surgery; delicate area with rare serious complications.
lead: Tear trough filler is the injection of a dermal filler, usually hyaluronic acid (HA), into the tear trough, the groove or hollow that runs from the inner corner of the eye diagonally down across the lower eyelid and upper cheek. Practitioners use it to soften the shadowed hollow and the tired appearance associated with infraorbital hollows, and some describe it as an alternative to lower eyelid surgery.
claims: Tear trough filler gives a noticeable correction without looking plastic

name: Cannula filler technique
summary: Blunt-tip filler placement through a flexible tube instead of a sharp needle; only small product-specific trials exist.
lead: The cannula filler technique is a method of placing injectable dermal filler through a blunt-tipped, flexible tube (a cannula) rather than a sharp needle. Practitioners typically make a single entry point in the skin and thread the cannula through the tissue to deposit product over a wider area. Fillers themselves are substances injected into skin or deeper tissue to smooth lines or add volume, and hyaluronic acid is the most common type .

name: Fraxel (Fraxel Restore / Dual)
summary: The original branded fractional laser for scars, photodamage and melasma, with decent small-study support and a multi-session, several-day recovery.
lead: Fraxel is a trademarked line of fractional laser systems for skin resurfacing, built on the principle of fractional photothermolysis: laser energy is delivered as an array of microscopic columns, leaving the skin between them untreated so that healing is faster than with full-surface lasers . Fraxel Restore and Fraxel Dual are non-ablative models using a 1550 nm erbium fiber laser, with the Dual adding a 1927 nm thulium wavelength for more superficial pigment targets .

name: Clear + Brilliant
summary: A mild "starter" fractional laser for tone and texture with minimal downtime; backed by small trials only.
lead: Clear + Brilliant is a non-ablative fractional laser by Solta Medical, marketed as a gentle, low-downtime resurfacing option for early signs of aging, with an original 1440 nm handpiece and a 1927 nm Perméa handpiece . It is often described as a "baby Fraxel" and is positioned as preventive skin maintenance .

name: Halo laser (hybrid fractional)
summary: A hybrid ablative/non-ablative fractional laser for photoaging and scars; only small registered studies are cited.
lead: Halo is a hybrid fractional laser, a category that combines an ablative and a non-ablative fractional wavelength in a single pass, aimed at photoaging, scars and pigment. Source material for this entry is thin, consisting of clinical trial registrations that name the Profile Halo mixed fractional laser or hybrid fractional lasers generally .

name: Fractional CO2 laser (CO2RE, Ultrapulse, SmartXide)
summary: The heavy-duty fractional laser for scars and deep wrinkles: best-studied, more downtime and risk than gentle lasers.
lead: Fractional CO2 laser resurfacing uses a 10,600 nm carbon dioxide laser, invented by C. Kumar N. Patel at Bell Labs in 1964 , in a fractional pattern that vaporizes microscopic columns of skin while leaving tissue between them intact. Commercial systems include CO2RE, UltraPulse and SmartXide.

name: Erbium YAG resurfacing
summary: A shallower, water-targeting resurfacing laser with less heat than CO2; skin evidence in the sources is thin.
lead: Erbium:YAG (Er:YAG) resurfacing uses a 2940 nm laser, strongly absorbed by water, to remove thin layers of skin for acne scars, deep wrinkles and melasma . Wikipedia says Er:YAG lasers carry a lower risk of hypopigmentation and scarring than CO2 lasers because they produce less heat .

name: Pico Genesis / PicoSure Pro
summary: Picosecond laser treatments for scars, pigment and skin texture; small published datasets so far, with the evidence still limited.
lead: PicoSure Pro is a picosecond laser system from Cynosure that emits light at 755 nm (an alexandrite laser) and can be fitted with a diffractive lens array. It is used in dermatology and aesthetic clinics for conditions such as atrophic acne scarring, wrinkles and pigmented lesions.

name: Ruby laser
summary: The first laser ever built, once used for tattoos, pigment and hair removal and now largely replaced by newer wavelengths.
lead: The ruby laser is a solid-state laser using a synthetic ruby crystal that emits pulsed red light at 694.3 nm. Theodore Maiman built the first working laser, a ruby laser, at Hughes Research Laboratories on 16 May 1960.

name: Alexandrite laser hair removal
summary: A 755 nm clinic laser for hair reduction, used mainly on lighter skin with dark hair; reduction, not total removal.
lead: Alexandrite laser hair removal uses a 755 nm laser, absorbed by melanin, to reduce dark hair through selective photothermolysis. Wikipedia lists alexandrite among the standard hair-removal lasers alongside ruby, diode and Nd:YAG.

name: Diode laser hair removal (LightSheer)
summary: The common 800-810 nm clinic hair-removal laser; LightSheer is a widely used brand with registered clinical trials.
lead: Diode laser hair removal uses semiconductor lasers around 800 to 810 nm to reduce hair by heating melanin in the follicle. Wikipedia lists pulsed diode arrays (810 nm) as suited to pale to medium skin.

name: Nd:YAG laser hair removal
summary: The 1064 nm laser used for hair reduction on darker skin tones, with deeper penetration and less surface melanin absorption.
lead: Nd:YAG laser hair removal uses a 1064 nm neodymium-doped yttrium aluminium garnet laser to reduce dark hair. Wikipedia lists it as the hair-removal laser for dark skin.

name: Soprano Ice laser
summary: A diode-type hair-removal system marketed as lower-pain; one small study of the triple-wavelength Platinum model in darker skin.
lead: The Soprano Ice Platinum from Alma Lasers (Germany) is a hair-removal laser that emits a combination of three wavelengths, 755, 810 and 1064 nm, in a single device.

name: GentleMax Pro
summary: Candela's alexandrite-plus-Nd:YAG clinic laser, mainly used for hair removal across skin tones; evidence is small studies and general hair-removal data.
lead: GentleMax Pro is a clinic laser platform made by Candela that combines a 755-nm alexandrite laser with a 1064-nm Nd:YAG laser in one device. It is used by dermatology and aesthetic practices, most commonly for laser hair removal, and its listed study conditions also include pigmented lesions, vascular lesions and pseudofolliculitis barbae (razor bumps). In looksmaxxing culture it falls under the hardmaxx category of professional procedures, usually discussed in connection with facial hair reduction.
